payload.title: PaMoDaCo: Contextualizing a downcore record in model-space
payload.summary: This Jupyter notebook explores the integration of multiple paleoclimate datasets to provide context for downcore records in model-space. It utilizes the iTRACE simulations to analyze abiotic and biotic components of radiocarbon data, focusing on the abiotic component. The notebook employs Xarray for efficient data handling and visualization, and compares model outputs with observational datasets such as Intcal20 and Marine20. The analysis includes plotting calibration curves and comparing them with data from Marchitto et al., 2007.
goals: Integrate multiple paleoclimate datasets for comprehensive analysis.
Analyze abiotic and biotic components of radiocarbon data.
Compare model outputs with observational datasets.
techniques: Data loading and indexing with Xarray

section_blurbs.blurb: The notebook aims to integrate multiple datasets for a comprehensive paleoclimate analysis, focusing on abiotic and biotic components of radiocarbon data from iTRACE simulations.
section_blurbs.heading: Overview

section_blurbs.blurb: Essential libraries such as Xarray, Matplotlib, and Pandas are imported for data handling, visualization, and analysis.
section_blurbs.heading: Imports

section_blurbs.blurb: The notebook addresses the hypothesis that CO2 accumulated in the deep ocean during the last glacial period and its release contributed to deglaciation.
section_blurbs.heading: Scientific Question

section_blurbs.blurb: Radiocarbon data from the C-iTrace project is loaded using Xarray, allowing for efficient data handling without loading the entire dataset into memory.
section_blurbs.heading: Load Data

section_blurbs.blurb: Initial exploration involves plotting sections from the Pacific and Atlantic to understand spatial and temporal aspects of the dataset.
section_blurbs.heading: Explore

section_blurbs.blurb: The notebook compares model outputs with observational datasets to validate the model's accuracy and reliability.
section_blurbs.heading: Model-Data Comparison

section_blurbs.blurb: Calibration datasets such as Intcal20 and Marine20 are loaded to provide a basis for comparison with model outputs.
section_blurbs.heading: Calibration Datasets

section_blurbs.blurb: Calibration curves are plotted to visualize changes in atmospheric radiocarbon over time, highlighting differences between datasets.
section_blurbs.heading: Plot

section_blurbs.blurb: Data from Marchitto et al., 2007 is loaded and plotted alongside model outputs to assess consistency and accuracy.
section_blurbs.heading: Marchitto et al, 2007

section_blurbs.blurb: The notebook integrates all datasets and model outputs to provide a comprehensive view of radiocarbon changes across different periods.
section_blurbs.heading: All together
